content.user_title: Create a tense astronaut survival opening
content.value_statement: Starting an interactive science-fiction survival scene can make it difficult to balance urgency, character, and player choice. This skill provides a structured first-contact scenario with dialogue beats, decisions, and future story hooks.
actual_capabilities: Establishes Stella Chen as a stranded astronaut with defined personality traits.
Guides a five-stage opening scene from distress call to overnight planning.
Offers three urgent choices with distinct short-term story outcomes.
Supplies sample bilingual Chinese-English dialogue for key moments.
Defines survival details, equipment, environmental hazards, and story hooks.
limitations: It is a fictional writing aid and does not provide real emergency or survival guidance.
It covers one opening chapter, not a complete campaign or game system.
The dialogue and setting focus on the named character and Gaia scenario.
It does not generate images, audio, or interactive game software by itself.

use_cases.title: Start a survival roleplay
use_cases.description: Open a one-on-one story with a clear emergency, a vulnerable protagonist, and meaningful choices.

use_cases.title: Draft a first chapter
use_cases.description: Use the scene structure to draft a tense science-fiction introduction with escalating stakes.

use_cases.title: Prototype narrative choices
use_cases.description: Adapt the three decision branches into early dialogue and consequences for a narrative game.

prompt_templates.title: Begin the distress call
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Emergency Distress Signal scene. Write Stella's first short message and ask me how I respond.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an urgent action
prompt_templates.prompt: Play Stella during the crashed-ship scene. Present the fire, oxygen leak, and communications problem, then give me three clear choices.

prompt_templates.title: Continue after evacuation
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue this scenario after Stella evacuates. Keep her bilingual voice, inventory her supplies, and ask me to choose shelter or water.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt Emergency Distress Signal into a new setting. Keep the five-stage structure, player choices, and gradual mystery, but create a different protagonist and planet.

output_examples.output: Stella sends a broken transmission, identifies herself, reports the crash, and asks whether anyone can hear her.

output_examples.input: I tell Stella to evacuate immediately.
output_examples.output: Stella grabs her survival pack, exits the damaged ship, and reports the alien forest, limited water, and a new decision.
Stella survives the evacuation, loses some equipment, builds trust with the player, and receives a lead toward shelter.

best_practices: Keep each response short so the player can make frequent choices.
Acknowledge the player's prior advice before presenting the next decision.
Maintain Stella's calm but vulnerable bilingual voice throughout the scene.
anti_patterns: Do not treat fictional hazards as real emergency instructions.
Do not make Stella solve every problem without player input.
Do not reveal every mystery of Gaia during the first chapter.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides an interactive opening scene about an astronaut surviving a crash on an unknown planet.

faq.question: Is this real survival advice?
faq.answer: No. The hazards, equipment, and decisions are fictional narrative elements.

faq.question: Which language does the character use?
faq.answer: Stella primarily speaks Chinese and mixes in English technical and casual terms.

faq.question: Can I change the player's decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to respond to player advice and branch around major choices.

faq.question: Can I reuse the structure for another story?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt its stages, pacing, and choice design to another character or setting.

faq.question: Does it include later chapters?
faq.answer: No. It recommends possible follow-up chapters but only defines the emergency opening chapter.
